name: Man or Astro-man?
label: Touch and Go
lede: Four Auburn students in space jumpsuits swore they were aliens sent to play surf music, then proved it with tesla coils, a dozen trips through John Peel's studio and two touring bands of clones.

eras.title: Transmissions from Auburn, Alabama
eras.text: Three Auburn University students came up through punk and fell for Dick Dale, The Ventures and the eerie echo of Outer Limits TV. They took stage names, put on jumpsuits and never admitted to being human. Within two years a garage label in Washington State and the BBC were on their side.

years.h: Man or Astro-man? plays its first show, in Birmingham
years.p: Brian Causey (Star Crunch), Brian Teasley (Birdstuff) and Robert Del Bueno (Coco the Electronic Monkey Wizard), all Auburn University students, debut in Birmingham, Alabama.
years.xp:
The name is widely believed to come from the U.S. poster for the Japanese sci-fi film The Human Vapor, which asked whether its villain was man or astro-man. The band has never publicly owned up to its members' real names, and sticks to the story that they are extraterrestrials sent to Earth to play surf music.

Jeff Goodwin joined soon after on second guitar as Dr. Deleto and His Invisible Vapotron.

years.h: Possession by Remote Control 7" on Homo Habilis
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s first single comes out on Homo Habilis Records, a label in the band's home town of Auburn, Alabama.

years.h: Is It... Man or Astroman? debut LP on Estrus
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s first album comes out on Estrus Records of Bellingham, Washington, the garage label that also issues the next two, stitched together with sound bites from obscure sci-fi films and TV.

years.src: Peel Wiki · Echoes and Dust interview with Brian Teasley
years.h: Man or Astro-man? records its first John Peel session
years.p: Teasley had once mailed John Peel a postcard, aged 19, asking him never to play the band. Peel booked them anyway; the session airs on BBC Radio 1 on January 22, 1994.
years.xp:
Teasley says the postcard was a hedge against being a one-session wonder. It didn't work: by the Peel Wiki's count the band recorded six Peel sessions between 1993 and 2000, and Peel said he'd played more records by them than by anyone except [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]].

For one late-1990s session the band swapped Peel's spoken introduction for a robot voice made with Mac software, without telling him. Teasley says Peel kept it on the broadcast.

eras.title: Surf music from Uranus
eras.text: Two more Estrus records and a road schedule that never let up. Man or Astro-man? became a fixture in the UK, and the shows grew into sci-fi stage sets with theremins, oscillators and, eventually, a tesla coil.

years.h: Destroy All Astromen!, second Estrus LP
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s second album for Estrus Records keeps the formula: early-'60s surf guitar, late-'70s punk and new wave drive, and B-movie dialogue between songs.

years.h: Project Infinity, last Estrus album of the first run
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s third Estrus album. The same year Live Transmissions from Uranus comes out on One Louder and Homo Habilis.

years.h: John Peel hangs out with Man or Astro-man? at the Phoenix Festival
years.p: At England's Phoenix Festival in 1995, Brian Teasley says, John Peel spent time with the band and found them funny. Their second Peel session had aired that April.

years.h: Cowboy Killers stop a Newport show to rescue the band's money
years.p: At TJ's in Newport, Wales, Man or Astro-man?'s merch money pouch fell off Brian Teasley's bass drum into the crowd. The Welsh band Cowboy Killers stopped everything to help get it back.

eras.title: Touch and Go, and the clones
eras.text: Touch and Go signed the band in 1996 and the records got stranger and more electronic. Cartoon Network hired them, Star Crunch walked out, and the band answered by training two extra touring versions of itself.

years.h: Experiment Zero, Man or Astro-man?'s Touch and Go debut
years.p: The Chicago label Touch and Go takes over as the band's home. Two more 1996 albums follow elsewhere: What Remains Inside a Black Hole (Au Go Go) and Intravenous Television Continuum (One Louder).

years.h: Third Peel session lands in Peel's Best 125
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s June 1996 BBC session, broadcast July 13, is later picked for Peel Sessions: The Best 125. The band named tracks after John Peel in three different sessions.

years.h: Made from Technetium on Touch and Go
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s second Touch and Go album, co-released with One Louder and Au Go Go, leans further into synths and electronics.

years.h: Man or Astro-man? scores Space Ghost Coast to Coast
years.p: For the 1997 season of Cartoon Network's Space Ghost Coast to Coast, the band records the closing theme and the interstitial music. The main theme is not theirs: it's credited to [[Sonny Sharrock|ebd39596-e2bb-4b3c-a661-412a4198a083]].

years.h: Star Crunch leaves Man or Astro-man? to run his label
years.p: Brian Causey quits to focus on his record label. He goes on to write and perform the theme for Nickelodeon's The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron, and runs Warm Electronic Recordings in Athens, Georgia.

years.src: Wikipedia · Encyclopedia of Alabama · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Clone Project Alpha: a second Man or Astro-man? goes on tour
years.p: Man or Astro-man? trains a whole second band to play its songs and sends it on the road as Clone Project Alpha, with renamed doubles of each member: Dorkstuff, Cocoid, Chromo Crunch and Dexter Y.
years.xp:
A second clone band, Clone Project Gamma, followed with an all-female line-up: Coco Active (Shonali Bhowmik), Chromia Staria (Deb Davis), Tweety-Tone (Ani Cordero) and Carol ([[Shannon Wright|d5fd4600-318d-457b-9cbb-b74633c51ed5]]). Brian Teasley calls it the Astro-man Genome Project.

Teasley admits fans first called it a cash grab. Now, he says, people claim to have been at shows they probably missed.

eras.title: The second model, and the shutdown
eras.text: Two clones, Blazar the Probe Handler and Trace Reading, joined the real band. They made a record with Steve Albini, toured it, and then switched the whole thing off.

years.h: EEVIAC Operational Index and Reference Guide
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s concept album about an imaginary computer, out on Touch and Go and Epitaph Europe and made by the band's post-Star Crunch line-up. Its fifth Peel session airs in July.

q: We weren't afraid to be thought of as good musicians
years.h: A Spectrum of Infinite Scale, produced by Steve Albini
years.p: Recorded with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] at Zero Return in Atlanta by Birdstuff, Coco, Blazar the Probe Handler (Richie Edelson) and Trace Reading (Erich Hubner), the last two recruited from the clone projects.
years.xp: Looking back on the record, Brian Teasley said the band had stopped hiding behind the kitsch and let the playing show.

years.h: Sixth Peel session, played live from Maida Vale
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s last session for John Peel is broadcast live from the BBC's Maida Vale studios on November 1, 2000.

years.src: Encyclopedia of Alabama · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Man or Astro-man? goes on hiatus after about 1,500 shows
years.p: After the Spectrum tour, sold with the tour-only A Spectrum of Finite Scale, the band stops. The Encyclopedia of Alabama counts over 1,500 shows in 31 countries since 1993.
years.xp:
The biggest crowd, the Encyclopedia of Alabama says, was 40,000 people at the Lowlands festival in the Netherlands. The smallest was two people, at an in-store in southern Australia. Teasley's own count in 2025 was bigger: more than 2,000 shows in over 40 countries, with more than two years of his life spent in the UK.

Estrus put out Beyond the Black Hole the same year.

eras.title: The astromen touch down again
eras.text: The original trio came back for a hometown show and Touch and Go's 25th birthday, then kept returning. Brian Teasley spent the break drumming for St. Vincent and The Polyphonic Spree and running a Birmingham club.

years.h: Original Man or Astro-man? reunites at the Bottletree Café
years.p: Star Crunch, Birdstuff and Coco, plus Dr. Deleto, play the Bottletree Café in Birmingham, Alabama, the club Brian Teasley ran until it closed in 2015.

years.h: Birdstuff gives his drums away at Touch and Go's 25th
years.p: At Touch and Go's 25th anniversary weekend in Chicago, Man or Astro-man? plays 45 minutes with a tesla coil, and Brian Teasley hands most of his drum kit to stunned fans.

years.h: Man or Astro-man? books Whirly Ball, Bottletree and SXSW
years.p: The trio announces 2010 dates at Whirly Ball in Atlanta, the Bottletree in Birmingham and South by Southwest, then plays Toronto's NXNE festival in June.

years.h: Avona Nova becomes the first woman in Man or Astro-man?
years.p: Samantha Paulsen joins on guitar as Avona Nova, replacing Victor Vector (Jonny Browning, 2010–11).

years.h: Defcon 5...4...3...2...1, first new music in 12 years
years.p: Man or Astro-man?'s comeback record comes out on Brian Causey's Warm Electronic Recordings and Chunklet Industries.

eras.title: Seventy songs in the can
eras.text: Man or Astro-man? now runs on its own clock. The live record came from Jack White's Nashville label, the Peel sessions came back on vinyl, and the drummer owns the venue.

years.h: Live at Third Man Records
years.p: Man or Astro-man? cuts a live album for [[Jack White|3ae2fb37-8a23-429d-9920-bac811c4fc22]]'s Third Man Records. Chunklet Industries later reissues the band's BBC sessions, including ROYGBIV (Recordings from the BBC).

years.h: Brian Teasley: 70 unfinished Man or Astro-man? songs
years.p: Teasley, who now owns the Saturn club in Birmingham, Alabama, tells Echoes and Dust the band has about 70 unfinished songs and plays when it feels like it.
